newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke says EMU start in '99 on the cards.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke says EMU start in '99 on the cards.

text.p: German Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that European Economic and Monetary Union could take place as targeted on January 1, 1999 without any softening of the Maastricht membership criteria.
Welteke went on to say the three percent government deficit target for EMU membership was not a make-or-break criterion.
"In my opinion, European currency union can start on January 1999, while conforming to those EMU convergence criteria that are most often discussed," said Welteke.

It was difficult to intellectually justify the difference between 2.9 percent and 3.1 percent when talking about government deficit to gross domestic product ratios, if the country had made big steps in getting close to the target.
"Fiscal stability in currency union is naturally a very important asset as it ensures that fiscal solidity of the individual members can be closely monitored," Welteke said.
A longer-term delay of EMU start increases danger that high levels of convergence could be weakened by market insecurity, Welteke said.
Welteke was unwilling to speculate on whether or not initial membership would be large or small
Welteke, who is also president of the Central Bank of the state of Hessen, was speaking at a dinner organised by the International Business Journalists Forum.
